## Natural history notes

A small leafhopper characterized by its slender wedge-shaped body, roof-like wings, and pale gold-and-white coloration that helps it blend into stems, leaves, and dried vegetation. In Florida, it is found in grassy or shrubby habitats such as fields, prairies, pine flatwoods, roadsides, gardens, and forest edges where suitable host plants occur. It feeds by piercing plant tissue and sucking sap, while also serving as prey for spiders, predatory bugs, birds, and other insect-eating animals.
